resources.allowTrivial: One reset per lifecycle step on this route: the opening frame, the height-only display resize at 20, the authored teleport at 24, the authored projection change at 28 and the input-only scale change at 32.
The reason is recorded per reset frame, so the display resize at 20 reports itself instead of the opening frame's own reason.
The authored FOV change at 28 requests no reset anywhere in the fixture, so this reason is the provider's own projection-discontinuity decision.
Only the input raster moves at 32, so the provider names the raster move itself.
Every reset after the opening counts the 1280x480 display the fixture resized to, so the GPU must report visiting that whole raster.
A reset frame carries no legal history at any pixel, so the whole counted display must be reported rejected.
The projection-change reset carries no legal history either, on the same counted display.
The input-scale reset carries no legal history either, on the same counted display.
One measured row per rendered frame; the row at the fixture's own frame 24 is the teleport frame.
The frame after the teleport must reuse history again, so the cut reset does not leak into the next frame.
The row at the fixture's own frame 28 is the authored projection change.
The frame after the projection change must reuse history again.
The row at the fixture's own frame 32 is the input-only scale change.
The frame after the input-scale change must reuse history again.
A frame that legitimately reuses history rejects only its own pixels, so the share is below the whole-raster reset value.
The input-only step must leave the physical display raster exactly where the height-only resize left it.
The authored half scale on the 1280-wide display is the 640-pixel input raster the lattice and the resolve must both follow.
One whole-display comparison per reset frame; the teleport frame is the third of them, and nothing later can change a recorded comparison.
The projection-change frame is the fourth whole-display comparison.
The input-only reset frame still compares every RGB channel of the unchanged 1280x480 display.
The same frame the lattice assertion below shares.
The lattice the scene drew on is the real 640x240 pass raster, not the display raster the scene never rendered into.
The lattice width is the input raster's, which is the raster the authored half scale produced.
A witness with no sample proves nothing, so the moving instance must be observed at least once before its error can be quoted.
The measured vector must exceed the fixture's 0.5-pixel moving threshold on at least one frame, so the reprojection being checked is real motion.
The measured MRT velocity must carry at least the moving threshold in pixels; a stationary vector would make the reprojection check vacuous.
The history coordinate the measured vector reprojects to must land within 0.05 pixel of the instance's independently projected previous location on every frame that reused history.
A witness with no sample proves nothing, so the skinned limb must be observed at least once.
The skinned limb's measured vector must exceed the fixture's 0.5-pixel moving threshold, so the bone history is under test rather than a frozen pose.
The skinned limb's measured MRT velocity must itself carry real motion, not a static pose's zero.
The skinned limb's reprojected history coordinate must land within 0.05 pixel of where the limb independently projected last frame on every frame that reused history.
The rigid body is the camera-independent control beside the two deforming and instanced points, held to the same 0.05-pixel bound.
The run settles on a frame that reuses history, so no reset gate is left engaged.
The applied stage list is decided when the chain is built, before the first observation.
The velocity route is decided when the chain is built, before the first observation, and the moving witnesses are read from that same attachment.
